comparisons.peer_summary: AMD continued investing in the open ROCm software stack, making key optimizations and adding features in the latest release to improve performance for generative AI workloads and simplify the developer experience.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Qualcomm disclose specific R&D investments focused on enhancing generative AI capabilities for their hardware platforms. Qualcomm describes conducting R&D to advance AI core capabilities to run on-device with a focus on power efficiency. Similarly, AMD details its continued investment in the ROCm software stack, specifically making optimizations to increase performance in generative AI workloads and simplify the developer experience for AMD platforms. While Qualcomm emphasizes the on-device execution and personalization aspects of its AI research, AMD highlights the software ecosystem (ROCm) and performance optimizations for training and inference, indicating a shared strategic focus on optimizing the software-hardware interface for generative AI workloads.

sentences.text: We conduct broad, leading research and development across AI, including generative AI, from fundamental research to platform and applied research, with the goal of advancing AI core capabilities to run on-device, and scaling them across industries and use cases.
With investments made in AI for over a decade, our research is diverse, and we are focused on power efficiency and personalization to make AI seamless across our everyday experiences.

We continued to invest in driving software capabilities and the open ecosystem to deliver powerful new features and capabilities in the AMD ROCm™ open software stack, bringing the latest features to highly-performant AI training and inference on AMD platforms.

During the year, we made several key optimizations and additional features in the latest AMD ROCm software that increases performance in key generative AI workloads, adds expanded support and optimization for additional frameworks and libraries, and simplifies the overall developer experience.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Tanzu Platform accelerates software delivery with enhanced governance and operational efficiency, includes Tanzu AI Solutions for generative AI applications, and offers full-stack visibility and lifecycle management across clouds.
comparisons.comparison: Both Broadcom and Qualcomm identify generative AI as a key area of technological focus and product development. Qualcomm states its R&D aims to advance AI core capabilities, including generative AI, to run on-device. Broadcom similarly highlights its Tanzu Platform, which includes 'Tanzu AI Solutions' specifically designed to help teams deliver 'generative AI-powered' applications. Both disclosures reflect a business strategy centered on enabling and optimizing generative AI applications, with Qualcomm focusing on the underlying on-device capabilities and Broadcom focusing on the software platform facilitating enterprise generative AI delivery.

sentences.text: We conduct broad, leading research and development across AI, including generative AI, from fundamental research to platform and applied research, with the goal of advancing AI core capabilities to run on-device, and scaling them across industries and use cases.

• Tanzu Platform: This cloud native application platform accelerates software delivery, providing platform engineering teams with enhanced governance and operational efficiency while reducing toil and complexity for development teams. Tanzu Platform includes access to content including enterprise-ready curated distributions of open source software technologies used for storing and processing data. It also includes Tanzu AI Solutions, a set of capabilities that help application teams deliver generative AI-powered, intelligent applications quickly, safely, and at scale. Tanzu Platform also offers teams full-stack visibility from applications to infrastructure and efficient modern application lifecycle management across public and private clouds with Cloud Foundry and/or with any conformant Kubernetes.

comparisons.peer_topic: Software strategy and open source contributions
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel aims to optimize AI frameworks and maintains the OpenVINO toolkit for deep learning inference. In 2024, Intel launched the Open Platform for Enterprise AI under the Linux Foundation and contributed oneAPI specifications to the UXL Foundation to enable open, multi-vendor programming across accelerators.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Qualcomm disclose active R&D efforts involving generative AI and open-source or open-standard frameworks to enhance performance on their respective hardware. Qualcomm emphasizes R&D in generative AI aimed at on-device execution and power efficiency. Intel describes optimizing AI frameworks (like PyTorch and vLLM) for its hardware and maintaining the open-source OpenVINO toolkit for deep learning inference, including generative AI use cases. Both companies are investing in software and platform capabilities to support generative AI workloads, though Qualcomm focuses on the on-device consumer experience while Intel focuses on cross-architecture optimization and open-source toolkits like OpenVINO.

sentences.text: We conduct broad, leading research and development across AI, including generative AI, from fundamental research to platform and applied research, with the goal of advancing AI core capabilities to run on-device, and scaling them across industries and use cases.

Our OpenVINO™ toolkit is an open source toolkit that accelerates deep learning inference on our processors across various use cases, such as generative AI, computer vision, audio, and language with industry standard models.
In 2024 we launched the Open Platform for Enterprise AI under the Linux Foundation to accelerate deployment of generative AI use cases through industry standard modular microservice architecture.
